title: Review: Combustion and fuels; Alcohols: production, dehydration and halogenation; Free-radical substitution
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR07#t2 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR07#t1 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN11#N.3, OR07#N.2, OR16#N.11, EN11#N.15, OR07#N.12, OR16#N.17, EN11#N.5, OR07#N.6, OR16#N.16, EN11#N.14, OR07#N.9, OR16#N.18b. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Homolytic fission
items.clue: A bond breaks so that one electron goes to each atom.

items.label: Complete combustion
items.clue: Burning in plenty of O₂, so that all C ends as CO₂ and all H as H₂O.

items.label: Radical
items.clue: A species with an unpaired electron, marked by a dot; highly reactive.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Colourless, odourless, toxic gas formed when a fuel burns in limited oxygen.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed.

questions.stem: Which statement about the chlorine radical, Cl•, is correct?

options.text: It has a 1− charge, which the dot is there to show.
It has eight outer electrons, all paired, like the chloride ion.
It is neutral, with seven outer electrons, one of them unpaired.
It is unreactive, as it has only one unpaired electron.

questions.explanation: Chlorine has seven outer electrons: three pairs and one unpaired electron. The dot marks the unpaired one. There is no charge.

questions.stem: Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, is heated with concentrated phosphoric acid. How many different alkenes can form?
questions.explanation: Losing H from C1 gives but-1-ene. Losing H from C3 gives but-2-ene, as both E and Z isomers.

questions.stem: After cooking outdoors, campers carry a still-glowing charcoal barbecue into their closed tent for warmth. Charcoal is almost pure carbon. Why is this deadly, even though there is no flame?

options.text: The charcoal burns to extra carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, which binds to haemoglobin in place of oxygen.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, an acidic gas that damages the lungs.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, which binds to haemoglobin.
The charcoal uses up all of the oxygen in the tent, and this lack of oxygen suffocates the campers.

questions.stem: The products of the reaction of methane with chlorine in UV light include CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄. How are most of these more highly substituted products formed?

options.text: Cl• removes an H atom from a chloromethane; the radical then reacts with Cl₂
Cl• replaces an H atom in a chloromethane directly, releasing a free H• radical
Chlorinated methyl radicals combine with Cl• in termination, the main source of products
Each forms in one step, e.g. CH₃Cl + Cl₂ → CH₂Cl₂ + HCl, as its equation shows

questions.explanation: Cl• attacks C–H bonds in chloromethanes as it does in methane: CH₃Cl + Cl• → CH₂Cl• + HCl, then CH₂Cl• + Cl₂ → CH₂Cl₂ + Cl•. Repeating gives CHCl₃ and CCl₄.

questions.stem: A few drops of an unknown colourless liquid are added to solid PCl₅. Steamy fumes appear. What can you conclude?

options.text: The liquid must be an alcohol.
The liquid contains a C=C bond.
The liquid contains an O–H group.

questions.explanation: PCl₅ swaps the OH for Cl and releases HCl, which fumes in moist air. Alcohols, acids and water all do this.

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, O₂, is needed to burn 0.500 mol of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH, completely?
questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH + 4½O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 10 O atoms; the alcohol supplies 1, so O₂ supplies 9: 4½ O₂ per mole. 0.500 × 4.5 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: Methane reacts with bromine in ultraviolet (UV) light. Which equation represents the initiation step?
questions.explanation: UV light breaks the Br–Br bond homolytically: one electron of the bonding pair goes to each atom, giving two bromine radicals.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol is warmed with potassium bromide and sulfuric acid. What is the main organic product?
questions.explanation: Br replaces the OH on the same carbon: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + HBr → CH₃CHBrCH₃ + H₂O.

questions.stem: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugar from sugar cane and is burned as a fuel for vehicles. Which statement about bioethanol as a fuel is correct?

options.text: It burns to form water only, so using it as a fuel adds no CO₂ to the atmosphere.
The CO₂ it releases is exactly balanced by photosynthesis, so its net emission is zero.
All of its carbon was fixed from atmospheric CO₂ by photosynthesis in the cane.
Its carbon was taken from the soil by the roots of the cane, not from CO₂ in the air.

questions.explanation: The cane took its carbon from the air within the last year or two. Even so, fossil fuels used to grow and process it add CO₂, so it is not carbon neutral.

questions.stem: 2,2-dimethylpropane, C₅H₁₂, reacts with chlorine in UV light. Four steps of the mechanism are: P: C₅H₁₁• + Cl₂ → C₅H₁₁Cl + Cl• Q: Cl₂ → 2Cl• R: C₅H₁₁• + Cl• → C₅H₁₁Cl S: C₅H₁₂ + Cl• → C₅H₁₁• + HCl Which sequence gives initiation, then the two propagation steps in the order they happen, then termination?
questions.explanation: Q makes Cl•. In S, Cl• removes an H atom, giving C₅H₁₁•. In P, that radical takes a Cl atom from Cl₂ and regenerates Cl•. R, two radicals combining, is termination.

questions.stem: Cyclopentanol is treated in two ways: (1) heated with concentrated phosphoric acid (2) warmed with potassium bromide and sulfuric acid What are the main organic products?
questions.explanation: In both, acid turns –OH into –OH₂⁺ and water leaves. With no halide present an H⁺ is lost (alkene); with Br⁻ present, Br takes the OH's place.
